paragraphs: We are a clinical-stage biotechnology company focused on developing next-generation precision medicines for large opportunities in targeted oncology and genetically defined conditions, harnessing the power of Fibroblast Growth Factor Receptor (FGFR) biology.

Our in-house precision medicine platform, SNÅP, enables rapid and precise drug design through iterative molecular SNÅPshots that help us design and predict which product candidates may demonstrate the highest potency, selectivity and tolerability in the clinic. Through this approach, we have built a wholly-owned pipeline of oral small molecule product candidates focused on targets that have previously been considered difficult-to-drug.
Our FGFR3 Programs—oral dabogratinib (formerly TYRA-300) for Urothelial Cancers and Skeletal Dysplasia

Alterations in the protein receptor FGFR3 are a validated driver in multiple indications with large market opportunities: urothelial cancers and skeletal dysplasia conditions. In urothelial cancer, uncontrolled activation of FGFR3 on the cell surface stimulates cellular proliferation. In skeletal dysplasia conditions, increased activity of FGFR3 expressed in growth plate chondrocytes (cartilage cells) results in excessive limitation of long bone growth.

Our lead program, oral dabogratinib, was designed to be more selective for FGFR3 over FGFR1, FGFR2, and FGFR4 to minimize off-target side effects, providing potential clinical advantages over less selective first-generation compounds and potentially addressing key unmet needs across both urothelial cancers and skeletal dysplasia conditions. To date, oral dabogratinib has been administered to over 100 participants across multiple clinical studies.

We demonstrated initial clinical proof-of-concept results with oral dabogratinib in the SURF301 study, a Phase 1 proof-of-concept study in metastatic urothelial carcinoma (mUC). Oral dabogratinib demonstrated encouraging anti-tumor activity and was generally well-tolerated, with infrequent FGFR2- and FGFR1-associated toxicities. Response, safety, pharmacokinetics (PK) / pharmacodynamics (PD) and circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) data from this study were leveraged to select doses that have the potential to achieve our target product profile for efficacy and safety in our Phase 2 trials and beyond.

We are currently advancing oral dabogratinib in three Phase 2 trials for three outsized market indications: SURF303, evaluating the treatment of low-grade upper tract urothelial carcinoma (LG-UTUC); SURF302, evaluating the treatment of intermediate risk non-muscle invasive bladder cancer (IR NMIBC); and BEACH301, evaluating the treatment of achondroplasia (ACH) in children. If we are successful with these Phase 2 studies, we expect to advance oral dabogratinib toward three potential registrational trials in LG-UTUC, IR NMIBC and ACH. We are calling this approach our "dabogratinib 3x3" strategy.

SURF303 for LG-UTUC: This open-label Phase 2a/b clinical trial was designed as a potential registrational trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of oral dabogratinib at doses of 60 mg and 80 mg once daily (QD) in participants with FGFR3-altered low-grade upper tract urothelial carcinoma, where approximately 85% of tumors are driven by FGFR3. Study startup is ongoing and the first patient in this study is anticipated to be dosed in 2026.

SURF302 for IR NMIBC: This open-label Phase 2 clinical trial is evaluating the efficacy and safety of oral dabogratinib at 50 mg and 60 mg QD in participants with FGFR3-altered low-grade, IR NMIBC, where approximately 70% of tumors are driven by FGFR3. We anticipate reporting initial three-month CR data from approximately 10-20 patients per cohort from this study by the end of the first half of 2026.

BEACH301 for ACH: This study is an open-label, Phase 2 dose-escalation/dose-expansion trial evaluating oral dabogratinib at lower doses (0.125, 0.25, 0.375, 0.50 mg/kg), as compared to the oncology studies, in children ages 3 to 10 with ACH with open growth plates, where approximately 99% of cases are driven by FGFR3. The study is enrolling a safety sentinel cohort of 3 or more participants per dose level in children ages 5 to 10, and a natural history run-in for cohorts 1 and 2 with children ages 3 to 10. Initial results from the safety sentinel cohort, including 6-month average height velocity (AHV) results and interim safety, are on-track and expected to be reported in the second half of 2026.

TYRA-430 was designed to be biased for FGFR4 and FGFR3 over the FGFR1 and FGFR2 isoforms specifically to address the FGF19 signaling pathway, while also potentially limiting side effects due to inhibition of FGFR1 and FGFR2, as well as to address acquired resistance mutations that have limited the efficacy of previous FGFR4-specific inhibitors. TYRA-430 is currently being evaluated in SURF431, a global, Phase 1, multicenter, open-label trial, with a focus on achieving clinical proof-of-concept in a cohort of patients with FGF19+ hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC).

TYRA-200 is an FGFR1/2/3 inhibitor designed to be active against nearly all of the clinically identified acquired resistant mutations that arise during treatment with pan-FGFR inhibitors, which we believe is necessary to address the problem of disease progression due to polyclonal resistance. TYRA-200 is currently being evaluated in SURF201, a global, Phase 1, multicenter, open-label trial, with a focus on achieving clinical proof-of-concept in a cohort of FGFR2-driven intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (ICC) resistant to previous FGFR inhibitors.

Our mission is to improve outcomes for patients living with cancer and genetically defined conditions. We are executing on our mission by focusing on advancing our pipeline and building a leading company around FGFR biology. With this strategy, our goal is the discovery, development and commercialization of next-generation precision small molecules against clinically validated targets to treat a wide range of indications currently lacking adequate treatment options.

headings: Summary of Risks Related to Our Business
Risks Related to Our Limited Operating History, Financial Position and Capital Requirements
We have incurred significant net losses in each period since our inception, and we expect to continue to incur significant net losses for the foreseeable future.

Our ability to generate revenue and achieve profitability depends significantly on our ability to achieve our objectives relating to discovery, development and commercialization of our product candidates.
Raising additional capital may cause dilution to our stockholders, restrict our operations or require us to relinquish rights to our technologies or product candidates.

Our portfolio of investments or bank deposits may be subject to market, interest and credit risk that may reduce their value and adversely affect our business, results of operations and financial condition.
Risks Related to the Discovery, Development and Marketing Approval of Our Product Candidates
As an organization, we have never completed any clinical trials or submitted an application for marketing approval and may be unable to do so for any of our product candidates.

Our proprietary SNÅP platform is innovative and unproven, and we do not know whether we will be able to develop any product candidates that are successful in clinical development or products of commercial value.
If we encounter difficulties enrolling patients in our clinical trials, our clinical development activities could be delayed or otherwise adversely affected.
paragraphs: You should carefully consider the following risk factors, together with the other information contained in this Annual Report, including our financial statements and the related notes and "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations," before making a decision to purchase or sell shares of our common stock. We cannot assure you that any of the events discussed in the risk factors below will not occur. These risks could have a material and adverse impact on our business, results of operations, financial condition and growth prospects. If that were to happen, the trading price of our common stock could decline. Additional risks and uncertainties not presently known to us or that we currently deem immaterial also may impair our business operations or financial condition. In this section, we first provide a summary of the principal risks and uncertainties we face and then provide a full set of risk factors and discuss them in greater detail.

• We are early in our development efforts, have a limited operating history, have not completed any clinical trials, and have no products approved for commercial sale, which may make it difficult for investors to evaluate our current business and likelihood of success and viability.
• We have incurred significant net losses in each period since our inception, and we expect to continue to incur significant net losses for the foreseeable future.

• Our ability to generate revenue and achieve profitability depends significantly on our ability to achieve our objectives relating to discovery, development and commercialization of our product candidates.

• We will require substantial additional capital to achieve our goals, and a failure to obtain this necessary capital when needed on acceptable terms, or at all, could force us to delay, limit, reduce or terminate our development programs, commercialization efforts or other operations.

• We are early in our development efforts, with three product candidates in clinical development, and our other development programs in the preclinical or discovery stage. If we are unable to successfully develop, obtain marketing approval and ultimately commercialize product candidates, or experience significant delays in doing so, our business will be materially harmed.

paragraphs: 本公司為一家臨牀階段的生物科技公司，專注於開發下一代精準醫療產品，以抓住針對性腫瘤治療及遺傳定義疾病領域的大型商機，運用纖維母細胞生長因子受體（FGFR）生物學的潛力。
我們的內部精準醫療平台 SNÅP，透過迭代式分子 SNÅPshots，使我們能快速且精準地設計藥物，協助我們設計並預測哪些產品候選藥物可能在臨牀上顯示出最高的藥效、選擇性與耐受性。透過此方法，我們已建立一個完全擁有之口服小分子產品候選藥物管線，專注於先前被認為難以開發的標的。
我們的 FGFR3 計畫—口服 dabogratinib（原為 TYRA-300）用於泌尿道癌及骨骼發育異常症狀
FGFR3 蛋白質受體的變異已被驗證為多種症狀領域的驅動因素，且具有大型市場商機：泌尿道癌及骨骼發育異常症狀。在泌尿道癌中，FGFR3 在細胞表面的不受控制活化會刺激細胞增殖。在骨骼發育異常症狀中，FGFR3 在生長板軟骨細胞（軟骨細胞）中表現出的活動增加，會導致長骨生長過度受限。
我們的領先計畫，口服 dabogratinib，是設計為對 FGFR3 的選擇性高於 FGFR1、FGFR2 和 FGFR4，以減少脫標副作用，提供潛在臨牀優勢，相比選擇性較低的第一代化合物，並可能解決泌尿道癌及骨骼發育異常症狀領域的關鍵未滿足需求。截至目前為止，口服 dabogratinib 已經給予超過 100 名參與者進行多項臨牀研究。

我們在 SURF301 研究中展示了口服 dabogratinib 的初步臨牀概念驗證結果，這是一個 Phase 1 概念驗證研究，用於治療轉移性泌尿道癌（mUC）。口服 dabogratinib 顯示出鼓舞人心的抗腫瘤活性，並普遍耐受良好，與 FGFR2 和 FGFR1 相關的毒性罕見。此研究的反應、安全性、藥動學（PK）/藥效學（PD）以及循環腫瘤 DNA（ctDNA）數據被用來選擇劑量，這些劑量有潛力實現我們在 Phase 2 研究及以後的目標產品特性（TPP）在療效與安全性方面的目標。

我們目前正推動口服 dabogratinib 進行三個 Phase 2 研究，針對三個規模龐大的市場指標：SURF303，評估治療低等級上泌尿道癌（LG-UTUC）；SURF302，評估治療中等風險非肌肉侵襲性膀胱癌（IR NMIBC）；以及 BEACH301，評估治療兒童的軟骨發育不全（ACH）。如果我們在這些 Phase 2 研究中取得成功，我們預期會將口服 dabogratinib 推進至三個潛在註冊研究，分別針對 LG-UTUC、IR NMIBC 和 ACH。我們將這種方法稱為我們的 "dabogratinib 3x3" 策略。
SURF303 用於 LG-UTUC：這是一個開放標籤的 Phase 2a/b 臨牀試驗，設計為潛在註冊試驗，用以評估口服 dabogratinib 在 60 mg 和 80 mg 一次每日（QD）劑量下，對 FGFR3 異常的低等級上泌尿道癌參與者的療效與安全性。試驗啟動工作正在進行中，預計在 2026 年會有第一個參與者接受治療。
SURF302 對 IR NMIBC：此為一項開放標籤的第二期臨牀試驗，評估口服 dabogratinib 50 mg 與 60 mg 每日一次在 FGFR3 異常的低階、IR NMIBC 受試者中的療效與安全性，其中約 70% 的腫瘤由 FGFR3 驅動。我們預期在 2026 年第一季末，根據此研究每組約 10 至 20 名受試者，報告初步三個月完全反應（CR）數據。

BEACH301 對 ACH：此研究為一項開放標籤、第二期劑量遞增/劑量擴展試驗，評估口服 dabogratinib 在較低劑量（0.125、0.25、0.375、0.50 mg/kg）下的效果，與癌症研究相比，用於 3 至 10 歲 ACH 且生長板未閉合的兒童，其中約 99% 的病例由 FGFR3 驅動。此研究正在招募每劑量層級 3 名或以上受試者之安全性哨兵組，並針對第一組與第二組進行自然病程篩選，年齡為 3 至 10 歲的兒童。安全性哨兵組的初步結果，包括 6 個月平均身高成長速率（AHV）結果與臨時安全性，預期在 2026 年第二季末報告。

TYRA-430 設計為針對 FGFR4 和 FGFR3，而非 FGFR1 和 FGFR2 等異構體，以針對 FGF19 信號路徑，同時也有可能透過抑制 FGFR1 和 FGFR2 來限制副作用，以及針對先前 FGFR4 特異性抑制劑所無法處理的獲得性抗藥性變異。TYRA-430 目前正在 SURF431 研究中評估，此為一項全球性、第一期、多中心、開放標籤試驗，重點在於於 FGF19+ 肝細胞癌（HCC）患者羣中實現臨牀概念驗證。
TYRA-200 是一項 FGFR1/2/3 抑制劑，設計為對幾乎所有臨牀上已識別的獲得性抗藥性變異有效，我們認為這是處理因多克隆抗藥性導致疾病進展問題所必需的。TYRA-200 目前正在 SURF201 研究中評估，此為一項全球性、第一期、多中心、開放標籤試驗，重點在於於 FGFR2 驅動的內臟膽管癌（ICC）患者羣中實現臨牀概念驗證，這些患者對先前 FGFR 抑制劑產生抗藥性。
我們的使命是改善患有癌症與遺傳性疾病患者的治療結果。我們透過專注於推進我們的藥物研發管道，並建立一間領導公司，聚焦於 FGFR 生物學，來執行此使命。透過此策略，我們的目標是發現、開發與商業化新一代的精準小分子藥物，針對已臨牀驗證的標的，用以治療目前缺乏足夠治療選擇的多種疾病。
我們實現此目標的策略要素為：

我們是一家臨牀階段生物技術公司，專注於開發下一代精準醫療產品，以應對目標性腫瘤學及遺傳定義疾病之重大市場機會，運用纖維母細胞生長因子受體（FGFR）生物學之力量。
我們內建之精準醫療平台SNÅP，透過迭代式分子SNÅPshots，使我們能快速且精準地設計藥物，協助我們設計並預測哪些產品候選藥物可能在臨牀中表現出最高的效力、選擇性與耐受性。透過此方法，我們已建立一個完全擁有之口服小分子產品候選藥物管線，專注於過去被認為難以開發之目標。
我們的FGFR3計畫—口服達博格拉汀（ formerly TYRA-300）用於泌尿道癌與骨骼發育異常症狀
FGFR3蛋白受體之變異已被驗證為多種具有重大市場機會之適應症之驅動因素：泌尿道癌與骨骼發育異常症狀。在泌尿道癌中，FGFR3在細胞表面之不受控制活化會刺激細胞增殖。在骨骼發育異常症狀中，FGFR3在生長板軟骨細胞（軟骨細胞）中之活動增加，會導致長骨生長過度受限制。
我們的領導計畫，口服達博格拉汀，是設計為對FGFR3比FGFR1、FGFR2及FGFR4更具選擇性，以減少離標副作用，提供潛在臨牀優勢，相比較少選擇性之第一代化合物，並可能解決泌尿道癌與骨骼發育異常症狀中關鍵未滿足之需求。截至目前為止，口服達博格拉汀已給予超過100位參與者參與多項臨牀研究。

我們在SURF301研究中，展示口服達博格拉汀之初始臨牀概念驗證結果，這是一個Phase 1概念驗證研究，用於治療轉移性泌尿道癌（mUC）。口服達博格拉汀顯示出鼓舞人心的抗腫瘤活性，並普遍耐受良好，與FGFR2及FGFR1相關之毒性罕見。此研究之反應、安全性、藥動學（PK）/藥效學（PD）及循環腫瘤DNA（ctDNA）數據被用來選擇劑量，這些劑量有潛力達成我們在Phase 2試驗及以後之目標產品特性（TPP）在療效與安全性方面之目標。

我們目前正推動口服達博格拉汀在三個Phase 2試驗中，針對三個規模龐大的市場適應症：SURF303，評估治療低等級上泌尿道癌（LG-UTUC）；SURF302，評估治療中等風險非肌肉侵襲性膀胱癌（IR NMIBC）；以及BEACH301，評估治療兒童之軟骨發育不全（ACH）。若我們在這些Phase 2試驗中成功，我們預期將推動口服達博格拉汀朝向三個潛在註冊試驗在LG-UTUC、IR NMIBC及ACH。我們將此方法稱為我們的『達博格拉汀3x3』策略。
SURF303 對 LG-UTUC：此為一項開放標籤的 Phase 2a/b 臨牀試驗，設計為潛在的註冊試驗，用以評估口服 dabogratinib 在 60 毫克及 80 毫克每日一次 (QD) 劑量下，對 FGFR3 異變之低階上泌尿道尿路上皮癌病患的療效與安全性，其中約 85% 的腫瘤是由 FGFR3 驅動。試驗啟動工作正在進行中，預計在 2026 年內首名病患將接受治療。
SURF302 對 IR NMIBC：此為一項開放標籤的 Phase 2 臨牀試驗，評估口服 dabogratinib 在 50 毫克及 60 毫克每日一次 (QD) 劑量下，對 FGFR3 異變之低階 IR NMIBC 病患的療效與安全性，其中約 70% 的腫瘤是由 FGFR3 驅動。我們預計在 2026 年第一季末，從此試驗中每組約 10 至 20 名病患的初步三月完全反應 (CR) 數據。

BEACH301 對 ACH：此試驗為一項開放標籤、Phase 2 劑量遞增/擴展試驗，評估口服 dabogratinib 在較低劑量 (0.125、0.25、0.375、0.50 毫克/公斤)，與癌症試驗相比，用於 3 至 10 歲 ACH 且生長板開放的兒童，其中約 99% 的病例是由 FGFR3 驅動。此試驗正在招募每劑量層級 3 名以上兒童的安全部門隊列，年齡為 5 至 10 歲，並針對第一及第二組隊列進行自然病程篩選期，年齡為 3 至 10 歲。來自安全部門隊列的初步結果，包括 6 個月平均身高成長速率 (AHV) 結果與臨時安全性，預計在 2026 年第二季內報告。

TYRA-430 設計為偏向 FGFR4 和 FGFR3，而對 FGFR1 和 FGFR2 等異構體則較不偏向，特別針對 FGF19 信號路徑，同時也有可能透過抑制 FGFR1 和 FGFR2 來限制副作用，以及針對先前 FGFR4 特異性抑制劑所無法處理的獲得性抗藥性變異。TYRA-430 目前正在 SURF431 試驗中評估，此為一項全球性、Phase 1、多中心、開放標籤試驗，重點在於於 FGF19+ 肝細胞癌 (HCC) 病患羣體中達成臨牀概念驗證。

TYRA-200 是一項 FGFR1/2/3 抑制劑，設計為對幾乎所有臨牀上已識別的獲得性抗藥性變異具有活性，這些變異會在使用廣泛 FGFR 抑制劑治療期間產生，我們認為這是處理因多克隆抗藥性導致疾病進展問題所必需的。TYRA-200 目前正在 SURF201 試驗中評估，此為一項全球性、Phase 1、多中心、開放標籤試驗，重點在於於 FGFR2 驅動之內臟膽管癌 (ICC) 病患羣體中達成臨牀概念驗證，這些病患對先前 FGFR 抑制劑產生抗藥性。
自 2018 年本公司開始營運以來，我們已將幾乎所有資源投入於組織與僱員配置、業務規劃、籌資、開發我們的專有 SNÅP 平台、進行我們開發計畫的研究與開發活動、建立我們的智慧財產權組合，以及提供一般及行政支援以支持我們的營運。截至目前為止，我們尚未產生任何收入，並主要透過我們的首次公開發行 (IPO)、私募發行可轉換優先股以及發行普通股及預資普通股權證來資助營運。

headings: 風險總覽：與我們業務相關的風險
與我們有限營運歷史、財務狀況及資金需求相關的風險
自我們成立以來，每個會計期間我們均產生顯著的淨虧損，且我們預期在可預見的未來仍將持續產生顯著的淨虧損。
我們產生收入並實現獲利的能力，很大程度上取決於我們達成與產品候選藥物的發現、開發及商業化相關目標的能力。
籌集額外資金可能會導致股東持股稀釋、限制我們的營運活動，或要求我們放棄對我們技術或產品候選藥物的權利。
我們的投資組合或銀行存款可能面臨市場、利率及信用風險，這些風險可能降低其價值，並對我們的業務、營運成果及財務狀況產生不利影響。
與我們產品候選藥物的發現、開發及市場批准相關的風險
作為一家公司，我們從來未完成任何臨牀試驗或提交過市場批准申請，且可能無法為任何產品候選藥物完成這些事項。
本公司自有智慧財產權 SNÅP 平台具創新性且尚未經驗證，我們無法確定是否能開發出在臨牀開發中成功的產品候選品或具商業價值的產品。
若我們在臨牀試驗中遇到招募病患的困難，將可能導致臨牀開發活動延遲或受到其他不利影響。
paragraphs: 您應謹慎考慮下列風險因素，並配合本年度報告中其他資訊，包括財務報表及相關附註，以及「管理層對財務狀況與營運結果之討論與分析」，以作為是否買進或賣出本公司普通股之決策依據。本公司無法保證下列風險因素中所討論之事件不會發生。這些風險可能對本公司之業務、營運結果、財務狀況及成長前景造成重大且不利的影響。若發生此類情況，本公司普通股之交易價格可能下跌。此外，尚有其他風險與不確定性，目前本公司尚未知悉，或認為不重要，也可能影響本公司之業務營運或財務狀況。在本節中，我們首先提供我們所面臨之主要風險與不確定性之總結，然後提供完整的風險因素並詳細討論。
• 我們目前仍處於發展初期，營運歷史有限，尚未完成任何臨牀試驗，且無任何產品已獲得商業銷售許可，這可能會使投資人難以評估我們目前之業務及成功與可持續性之可能性。
• 自我們成立以來，每個會計期間我們均產生顯著之淨虧損，且我們預期在可預見之未來仍將持續產生顯著之淨虧損。
• 我們產生收入並實現獲利之能力，很大程度上取決於我們達成與產品候選藥物之發現、開發與商業化目標之能力。
• 我們將需要大量額外資金以實現目標，若無法在需要時以可接受之條件或完全無法取得此必要資金，可能會迫使我們延遲、限制、減少或終止我們之發展計畫、商業化努力或其他營運活動。
• 我們目前仍處於發展初期，有三種產品候選藥物正在進行臨牀開發，且其他發展計畫處於臨牀前或發現階段。若我們無法成功開發、取得市場核准並最終商業化產品候選藥物，或遭遇顯著之延遲，將對我們之業務造成重大損害。
